name: Astrid Carolina Herrera
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Miss World 1984 pageant in London on November 15, 1984, becoming the third Venezuelan to win the title.
early_history_summary: Born in Yaracuy, Venezuela, Herrera competed as Miss Miranda in Miss Venezuela 1984, earning the Miss World Venezuela title. She then represented Venezuela at the Miss World 1984 pageant in London, where she won the Photogenic award, Miss World Americas, and was crowned Miss World 1984 at age 21.
family_context_summary: Born to David Herrera and Odelia Irazábal in Yaracuy, Venezuela; third of six children. Parents supported her early interest in public speaking and performance.
primary_early_advantage_tags: beauty pageant pipeline, Venezuelan pageant ecosystem, physical appearance
evidence_summary: Herrera won Miss World 1984 at age 21, leveraging Venezuela's renowned pageant pipeline. Born to a family in Yaracuy with supportive parents, she entered the Miss Venezuela system and won the international title. The Venezuelan pageant ecosystem was a well-oiled machine in the 1980s, providing training, exposure, and a national platform. No evidence of family wealth or domain expertise in entertainment was found.
starting_point: Born to David Herrera and Odelia Irazábal in Yaracuy, Venezuela; third of six children in a middle-class family.
current_position: Former Miss World and Venezuelan telenovela actress; estimated net worth ~$5 million; resides in Venezuela; last credited acting role in 2011.

trajectory.event: Crowned Miss World 1984 in London, becoming the third Venezuelan to win the title.
Debuted as actress in the telenovela 'Mi amada Beatriz' on RCTV.

Landed first leading role in the telenovela 'Alma mía' on RCTV.
Played prominent role in the telenovela 'Amantes de Luna Llena'.
Final acting role as Ivana Humboldt in the telenovela 'La viuda joven'.
Gave birth to her first child, Miranda Carolina Herrera Irazábal, at age 50.

name: Bora Milutinović
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Yugoslav First League championship with Partizan Belgrade in 1963 at age 19, and again in 1965; reached the European Cup final in 1966 as part of the 'Partizan's Babies' generation.
early_history_summary: Orphaned during WWII and raised by an aunt in Bajina Bašta, Serbia, Milutinović followed his older brothers Milos and Milorad to Partizan Belgrade at age 17. He joined the famous 'Partizan's Babies' generation that dominated Yugoslav football in the 1960s, winning league titles in 1963 and 1965 and reaching the 1966 European Cup final.
family_context_summary: WWII orphan raised by an aunt in the Serbian town of Bajina Bašta. Two older brothers, Milos and Milorad, also played football at Partizan Belgrade.
parent_family_domain_summary: Older brothers Milos and Milorad were footballers at Partizan Belgrade, providing a direct family pipeline to top-level Yugoslav football.
primary_early_advantage_tags: brothers at Partizan, orphan adversity, Yugoslav football pipeline, early specialization, Partizan's Babies
evidence_summary: Milutinović was a WWII orphan who followed two older brothers to Partizan Belgrade at 17, joining the 'Partizan's Babies' generation that won Yugoslav championships in 1963 and 1965 and reached the 1966 European Cup final. His family pipeline to one of Europe's top clubs was the dominant early advantage. He played 210 games for Partizan before embarking on a globe-trotting playing and coaching career.
starting_point: WWII orphan raised by an aunt in Bajina Bašta, Serbia; two older brothers played football at Partizan Belgrade.
current_position: Retired Serbian football manager; age 81; served as ambassador for the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar; most famous for coaching five different national teams at World Cups.

trajectory.event: Won Yugoslav First League championship with Partizan Belgrade as part of the 'Partizan's Babies' generation.
Won second Yugoslav First League championship with Partizan.
Reached European Cup final with Partizan, losing to Real Madrid.
Became head coach of UNAM Pumas in Mexico, transitioning to management.
Led Mexico to World Cup quarter-finals as host nation, the country's best-ever finish.
Coached the United States national team at the 1994 World Cup.
Coached China at the 2002 World Cup, his fifth different national team at a World Cup.

name: Ashot Anastasian
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Armenian Chess Championship in 1983 at age 19, and repeated in 1985, 1986, 1987, and 1988, establishing dominance in Armenian chess well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Yerevan, Armenian SSR, Anastasian emerged through the Soviet chess pipeline. He won the Armenian Chess Championship for the first time in 1983 at age 19 and dominated the championship through the 1980s, winning it five times before age 26. He received the International Master title in 1988.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet chess pipeline, Armenian championship dominance, early specialization
evidence_summary: Anastasian won the Armenian Chess Championship at age 19 in 1983 and dominated it through the 1980s, winning five times before 26. He benefited from the Soviet chess infrastructure in Armenia, though specific family background and coaching details are not documented in reviewed sources. He later earned the IM title in 1988 and GM title in 1993.
starting_point: Born in Yerevan, Armenian SSR, Soviet Union; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died December 26, 2016 at age 52; final role: coach of the Armenian national women's chess team, appointed in 2010.

trajectory.event: Won the Armenian Chess Championship for the first time.
Received the International Master title and won the Armenian Championship for the fifth time.
Awarded the Grandmaster title and won tournament in Katowice.
Won individual gold medal at the Chess Olympiad.
Won the Armenian Chess Championship for the eighth time.
Appointed coach of the Armenian national women's chess team.
Died on December 26, 2016.

name: Eduardo Galeano
milestone_by_age_26: Became editor-in-chief of Marcha, Uruguay's most influential weekly magazine, by 1961 at age 21, later directing the daily Época and serving as editor-in-chief of the University Press.
early_history_summary: Born in Montevideo to a prominent family descended from Uruguay's first president, Galeano dropped out of secondary school after two years and began working at age 14. He published cartoons in the socialist weekly El Sol as a teenager and rose rapidly through leftist journalism, becoming editor of Marcha by age 21.
family_context_summary: Born to a prominent Uruguayan family; father was a civil servant at the Ministry of Livestock and owned a ranch. Descended from Fructuoso Rivera, first president of Uruguay, through maternal line, and from military leader Leandro Gómez through paternal line.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family was politically and culturally connected in Uruguay, though not directly in journalism. The family's social standing provided access to intellectual circles.
primary_early_advantage_tags: prominent family, Marcha editorship, Uruguayan intellectual circles, early journalism start, political connections
evidence_summary: Galeano came from a prominent Uruguayan family descended from the country's first president, which provided cultural capital and social access. He began working in journalism at 14, publishing cartoons in El Sol, and rose to editor-in-chief of Marcha by 21, an influential weekly with contributors like Vargas Llosa. His family's social standing and Montevideo's intellectual ecosystem facilitated his rapid rise in Latin American leftist journalism.
starting_point: Born to a prominent Uruguayan family in Montevideo; father was a civil servant and ranch owner; descended from Uruguay's first president Fructuoso Rivera.
current_position: Died April 13, 2015 at age 74 in Montevideo; final role: celebrated writer and journalist, author of Open Veins of Latin America and Memory of Fire trilogy.

trajectory.event: Became editor-in-chief of Marcha, Uruguay's most influential weekly magazine.
Became director of the daily Época and editor-in-chief of the University Press.
Published Open Veins of Latin America, his most famous and influential work.
Imprisoned during Uruguay's military coup; fled to Argentina and founded Crisis magazine.
Published first volume of Memory of Fire trilogy while in exile in Spain.
Returned to Montevideo after the end of the military dictatorship.
Died of lung cancer on April 13, 2015 in Montevideo.

name: Silvana Mangano
milestone_by_age_26: Starred in Bitter Rice (Riso Amaro, 1949) at age 19, a landmark of Italian neorealist cinema that made her an international star; signed contract with Lux Film the same year.
early_history_summary: Born in Rome to a railway worker father and an English mother, Mangano grew up in poverty during WWII. She trained as a dancer for seven years and worked as a model. At 16, she won the Miss Rome beauty pageant, which led to film roles. Her breakthrough came with Bitter Rice (1949), which became one of the most iconic images of postwar European cinema.
family_context_summary: Born in Rome to an Italian railway worker father and an English mother (Ivy Webb from Croydon). Grew up in poverty during World War II.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family connections to film or entertainment industry. Father was a railway worker.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wartime poverty, dance training, Miss Rome, Italian neorealist cinema, Rome film ecosystem
evidence_summary: Mangano grew up in wartime poverty in Rome, training as a dancer for seven years and working as a model. At 16, she won Miss Rome, which opened doors to film. Her breakthrough in Bitter Rice (1949) at age 19 made her an international star of Italian neorealist cinema. Her physical talent, dance training, and proximity to Rome's film industry were key advantages, while poverty created urgency to work early.
starting_point: Born in Rome to an Italian railway worker and an English mother; grew up in poverty during World War II.
current_position: Died December 16, 1989 at age 59 in Madrid, Spain; final film role was in Dark Eyes (1987).

name: Valery Salov

early_history_summary: Born in Wrocław, Poland, Salov trained under renowned Leningrad coach Vladimir Zak at the Leningrad Pioneers' Palace. He won the World Under-17 Championship at 16 and the European Junior Championship at 19-20, earning the IM title in 1984 and GM title in 1986.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Vladimir Zak coaching, Leningrad Pioneers' Palace, Soviet chess pipeline, World U-17 champion, early GM title
evidence_summary: Salov trained under renowned coach Vladimir Zak at the Leningrad Pioneers' Palace, a key Soviet chess development institution. He won the World U-17 Championship at 16 and European Junior Championship at 19-20, earning the GM title at 22. The Soviet chess pipeline and dedicated coaching from a young age were the dominant early advantages. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Wrocław, Poland; trained in Leningrad under coach Vladimir Zak; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Inactive from FIDE-rated chess since January 2000; former world No. 3 (1995); current whereabouts and occupation unknown.

name: Sergei Skripal
